No section of the math-foundations document mentions Bloodsong, Expose Weakness, support damage multipliers, or the melee/ranged split (grep for 'bloodsong|expose weakness|support_damage|melee|ranged|{{rd' returns zero hits). The document therefore neither supports nor contradicts this leaf; the wiki cache is the sole numeric source.

independent_computation.step_1_effect_exists: The cached Bloodsong wiki text states the debuff explicitly amplifies damage 'from all sources', not merely the holder's. In a coupled/roster ledger, an ally's (or the subject's) damage event landing inside the 4 s Expose Weakness window must therefore carry an amplification factor. A total absence of the leaf is equivalent to multiplier = 1.00, i.e. no amplification at all, which contradicts the item text.
independent_computation.step_2_decode_template: The value is written {{rd|8%|5%}}. The {{rd|...}} template is the League Wiki melee/ranged split, first argument melee, second ranged. Decoded from the same cache without outside knowledge: (a) Hullbreaker writes the second argument literally as the first times 0.7 ({{rd|120%|{{ap|120*0.7}}%}}, {{rd|5%|{{ap|5*0.7}}%}}, {{rd|300%|{{ap|300*0.7}}%}}); (b) Kraken Slayer and Immortal Shieldbow write the second argument as the first times 0.8; (c) Titanic Hydra writes {{rd|1%|{{fd|0.5}}%}} and {{rd|3%|{{fd|1.5}}%}}, i.e. exactly half. In every case the second argument is the systematically reduced value, which is the ranged-holder value in League's melee/ranged item convention (cross-checked against the well-known live splits: BORK 9% melee / 6% ranged, Death's Dance 30% melee / 10% ranged, Ravenous & Titanic Hydra cleave 40%/20% and 1%/0.5%). Argument order is therefore melee | ranged.
independent_computation.step_3_value: Expose Weakness damage amplification = 8% if the Bloodsong holder is melee, 5% if ranged.
independent_computation.step_4_multiplier_form: The leaf encodes a factor, so multiplier = 1 + amp: melee 1 + 0.08 = 1.08; ranged 1 + 0.05 = 1.05. The published new value 1.08 equals the melee-holder value exactly.
independent_computation.step_5_window_check: The amplification is windowed (4 s of Expose Weakness, applied only after the empowered on-hit lands on a champion, 1.5 s internal cooldown starting after the empowered attack). The leaf appearing on a single event (events[39]) rather than on every event is consistent with a windowed application; the per-event membership itself is engine timing that this evidence tree cannot adjudicate.
independent_computation.conclusion: 1.08 is the correct value for a melee Bloodsong holder and is the only value between the two admissible ones that the change could plausibly intend; the previous state (leaf absent, i.e. 1.00) is unambiguously wrong because the cached item text amplifies damage from all sources.

caveats: The scenario roster for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' is defined outside the permitted evidence tree (nothing under data/ names the scenario; data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json does not contain it). I therefore could not confirm from the allowed sources that the Bloodsong holder in this roster is melee.

Conditional statement of the result: if the Bloodsong holder is melee, 1.08 is exactly right. If the holder is a ranged champion, the correct value would be 1.05 and the verdict would flip to both_wrong. The absent (1.00) state is wrong in either case.

Aside (out of scope for this leaf, flagged for the maintainer): data/champions.json documents a Gangplank-specific exception — 'Bloodsong: Dealing damage with kegs to champions won't apply Expose Weakness to them.' Any scenario whose Spellblade proc is carried by a Gangplank keg must not author this multiplier.
